title: PROOF-Gen: From Optimized Data to Better Distillation
gist: Apple researchers introduce PROOF-Gen, a per-scenario prompt-optimization method that recovers 93% of failed teacher trajectories in tool-calling distillation (where 57% of teacher trials fail on tau2-bench), producing measurable gains in both open-weight models (Qwen3-4B, Gemma 4 E4B) and a deployed on-device Apple model across every tested locale.

themes.theme: The inefficiency of standard teacher-distillation pipelines

insights.claim: Shipped tool-calling agents are typically refreshed via post-training pipelines that re-run supervised fine-tuning on frontier-teacher-generated trajectories on a daily or weekly cadence, meaning the expensive frontier-teacher inference cost is paid repeatedly every cycle.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Frontier-teacher API/compute cost is a recurring, non-trivial operating expense for any company running production distillation refresh cycles for agentic AI products, not a one-time training cost.
insights.quote: Post-training pipelines that drive shipped tool-calling agents re-run this stage on a daily or weekly cadence, paying the frontier-teacher cost each cycle

insights.claim: The standard generate-and-filter distillation mechanism keeps only the teacher's passing trajectories and discards failures, so each refresh cycle leaves the same hard scenarios unsolved because failed attempts provide no training signal.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Identifies a structural inefficiency in industry-standard distillation: recurring cost is spent without closing the gap on persistently hard cases, which is exactly the inefficiency PROOF-Gen targets.
insights.quote: the mechanism is generate-and-filter (keep the teacher's passing trajectories, discard the rest) and each cycle leaves behind the same hard scenarios because failures supply no signal

insights.claim: On the tau2-bench tool-calling benchmark, 57% of teacher-model trials fail, and two-thirds of those failures are near-misses where most tool calls were correct but a single decisive error caused failure.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Quantifies that a majority of 'failed' teacher trajectories are nearly correct and thus recoverable, which is the empirical justification for building a recovery method instead of just discarding them.
insights.quote: On τ 2-bench, 57% of teacher trials fail, two-thirds of them near-misses (most tool calls correct, undone by one decisive error).

insights.claim: PROOF-Gen (Per-scenario Reflective Optimization to Overcome Failed Generation) recovers golden trajectories from teacher failures via per-scenario prompt optimization rather than discarding them, treating failed attempts as a recoverable data source instead of waste.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Reframes a common industry practice (discard failed generations) as leaving value on the table; teams running distillation pipelines could extract meaningfully more usable training data per teacher-inference dollar spent.
insights.quote: We introduce PROOF-Gen (Per-scenario Reflective Optimization to Overcome Failed Generation), which recovers golden trajectories from these failures via per-scenario prompt optimization.

insights.claim: For each failed task, a 'reflector' component analyzes the execution trace and evaluation feedback, then writes corrective guidance that steers the teacher model to a passing trajectory; this guidance is stripped before training so the student model learns from clean demonstrations without any task-specific scaffold leaking into its training data.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The strip-before-training design is a reusable architectural pattern for avoiding contamination when using self-correction or hint-based methods to generate distillation data.
insights.quote: For each failed task, a reflector analyzes the execution trace and evaluation feedback, then writes corrective guidance that steers the teacher to a passing trajectory. The guidance is stripped before training, so the student learns from clean demonstrations with no task-specific scaffold.

insights.claim: Per-scenario prompt optimization recovers 93% of the previously failed scenarios on tau2-bench, converting most 'wasted' teacher trials into usable training trajectories.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A 93% recovery rate on failures implies a large multiplier on effective usable training data from the same amount of teacher compute, directly lowering the cost-per-usable-trajectory of distillation.
insights.quote: On τ 2-bench, per-scenario optimization recovers 93% of failed scenarios.

themes.theme: Measured performance gains, including in production

insights.claim: Fine-tuning Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on the PROOF-Gen-augmented data improved its Pass^1 score on tau2-bench from 0.132 to 0.529, roughly a 4x improvement.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A ~4x jump in a small (4B) open-weight model's tool-calling accuracy from better training data alone (no architecture change) shows data-quality interventions can rival or exceed gains from scaling model size.
insights.quote: Fine-tuned on the combined data, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 improves from Pass^1=0.132 to 0.529

insights.claim: Gemma 4 E4B-it gains 7.2 percentage points on the BFCL v4 multi-turn benchmark after training on PROOF-Gen data.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Confirms gains generalize across at least two different open-weight model families (Qwen and Gemma), suggesting the method is model-agnostic rather than a one-off tuning artifact.
insights.quote: Gemma 4 E4B-it gains +7.2pp on BFCL v4 multi-turn

insights.claim: In a live deployed pipeline, PROOF-Gen lifts trajectory quality by 6.3 percentage points in goal completion, and the improvement transfers to a deployed on-device model with a 1.5 percentage point goal-completion gain and 1.7-5.0 percentage point gains across response-quality metrics, with positive transfer in every tested locale (non-English locales averaging +1.48pp).
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: This is a production result, not just a benchmark paper: Apple is already using this technique to improve a shipped on-device agent, with gains holding across languages/locales, which is a concrete efficiency lever behind Apple's on-device AI quality roadmap.
insights.quote: In a deployed pipeline, the method lifts trajectory quality by +6.3pp goal completion and transfers to a deployed on-device model (+1.5pp goal completion; +1.7 to +5.0pp across response-quality metrics), with positive transfer in every locale (non-English average +1.48pp).

insights.claim: A related Apple research thread on on-policy distillation for reasoning models notes it remains unclear which teacher model to use, or in self-distillation which specific context should serve as the supervisory signal, and whether the optimal choice varies token by token — an open problem distinct from PROOF-Gen's tool-calling focus.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Signals Apple is investigating multiple unresolved dimensions of distillation design (teacher choice, token-level signal selection) beyond tool-calling, indicating a broader research bet on distillation efficiency across model types.
insights.quote: it remains unclear under which conditions this signal is beneficial and under which it is detrimental. Which teacher model should be used, and in the case of self-distillation, which specific context should serve as the supervisory signal?
insights.locator: related paper teaser, undated on-policy distillation entry

insights.claim: A separate Apple ICML 2025 paper proposes a distillation scaling law that estimates distilled-model performance from a compute budget and its allocation between student and teacher, providing compute-optimal recipes for both when a teacher already exists and when one must be trained.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A formal scaling law for compute allocation between teacher and student gives practitioners a way to budget distillation runs optimally, directly relevant to cost planning for any team building distilled production models.
insights.quote: We propose a distillation scaling law that estimates distilled model performance based on a compute budget and its allocation between the student and teacher.
